newsitem.title: CANADA: Consolidated Eurocan up during road show.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Eurocan up during road show.

text.p: Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd was popular with investors on Friday, rising in heavy trading on interest generated from an ongoing road-show.

"There's no news, but they are on a financial road show, which is raising the profile," spokeswoman Sophia Shane said in an interview from the company's head office in Vancouver. Shares were up C$0.35 to C$6.60 in mid-day trading, approaching a 52-week high of C$6.75. More than 350,000 shares traded hands.
Company executives were in New York on Thursday and are now heading off to London, Stockholm and Paris, Shane said.
Consolidated Eurocan and its advisers are marketing 23.5 million special warrants on a best efforts basis. The company plans to raise C$120 million.
The shares are oversubscribed even though the closing date is still a few weeks away, Shane said.
Consolidated Eurocan claims it has the rights to the Tenke-Fungurme copper and cobalt deposit in Zaire, based on an agreement with Zairean President Mobuto Sese Seko.

But a group of companies led by Cornucopia Resources Ltd and its two giant partners, Inco Ltd and Phelps Dodge Corp, have said the country's prime minister and his minister of mines has invited them to assess the mine.
Consolidated said it hopes to have a finalized written agreement within a couple of weeks.
